Subject: Dedicated capacity post-call recap - Orion Health

Alex, great to meet you and Priya earlier. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we stay aligned:

Summary of pain points
- High variability in inference traffic across appointment windows driving unpredictable token costs.
- Regulatory requirement for data isolation for PHI workloads (cannot co-mix with multi-tenant hosted).
- Strict SLA target for 99.9% inference availability during business hours and sub-200ms P95 latency for core flows.
\Goals you shared
- Reserved capacity (dedicated GPUs) for production LLM inference for clinical QA and triage.
- Ability to scale up for monthly peak windows (end of month claim processing) and burst for daily peak hours.
- Audit logs and KMS integrations for full compliance.
\What Redwood proposes (high-level)
- Dedicated capacity pool (reserved GPUs) in a customer-isolated tenant with KMS integration and audit logs.
- Autoscaling policy that maintains baseline nodes for 99.9% availability and adds burst nodes for spikes (configurable).
- SLA target: 99.9% uptime, P95 latency goal of <200ms for short-text clinical prompts; verified during canary.
\Immediate next steps
1) I will share an SOW draft and capacity worksheet (attached) - please confirm traffic profile and peak RPS by next Wed (2027-07-01).
2) Marissa will follow up with a technical plan and required VM/GPU sizing.
3) Your security/compliance team to send the completed questionnaire (attached) or any missing items.
\Attachments: SOW_draft_Orion_Health.docx, capacity_estimate.csv, orion_security_questionnaire_v2.pdf
\Thanks, I'll coordinate with Marissa to get the technical sizing and a proposed rollout timeline.
\Best,
Ben

Thanks Ben, appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- Isolation: We need tenant-level isolation and proof that no other customer workloads can access our KV cache or model artifacts.
- Data residency: Primary region must be us-west-2 for this pilot; possible eu region for redundancy later.
- Compliance checklist: We completed most of the questionnaire; I attached our internal compliance note and marked two open items (keys rotation and long-term logs retention).
\Traffic profile (rough)
- Baseline: 6 RPS average across clinical flows
- Peak: spikes to ~40 RPS during daily processing windows (15-30 minute bursts)
- Monthly batch: a 4-6 hour window where throughput may increase to sustained 80 RPS for batched report generation
\Timeline: We're targeting a pilot kickoff in mid-July, production by end of August if the SOW and security checks are green.
\I attached the questionnaire (orion_security_questionnaire_v2.pdf) and an internal infra note. Priya, feel free to add anything I missed.
\Best,

Alex / Ben, thanks for the notes. I put together a proposed technical approach below and a couple of questions so we can size reserved capacity accurately.
\Proposed technical approach
- Dedicated capacity: customer-isolated VPC with dedicated GPU pool (NVIDIA H100 / A100 options depending on model footprint).
- Autoscaling: baseline of N nodes (keeps KV cache warm), additional burst nodes with cold-start mitigations and fast warm-up using cached prefixes.
- KV cache and model artifact isolation: per-tenant storage and explicit ACLs; logs written to customer-controlled S3 with audit metadata.
- KMS integration: support for AWS KMS/HSM; we can review key rotation cadence and access control.
\Sizing questions (please confirm):
1) Average sequence length for clinical prompts (typical tokens) - this changes per-GPU throughput estimates.
2) Desired concurrency per request (do you send many small parallel requests or longer batched requests?).
3) Any hard upper limit for cost or node count for the pilot phase?
\SLA and rollout
- We can commit to a pilot SLA target of 99.9% for availability and will instrument P95 latency tracking. We recommend a 2-week canary with live traffic (non-critical flows) to validate <200ms P95.
- Rollout plan: 2-week pilot -> extend capacity and fine-tune autoscaling -> production cutover.
\I attached a quick capacity_estimate.csv with initial node counts for H100/A100 based on Alex's spike numbers; it's a conservative starting point. Ben, once we have avg sequence length and concurrency, I'll update the sheet and SOW.
\Marissa

Thanks Marissa, that plan looks good. Quick answers to your sizing questions:

1) Average sequence length: 160 tokens for clinical QA flows, 450 tokens for batch report generation.
2) Concurrency: most requests are single-threaded per user; during spikes we see many parallel short requests, roughly 1-2 tokens per request average concurrency 40-60 concurrent small requests at peak.
3) Cost ceiling for pilot: $35k/month preferred, but we can be flexible if ROI is clear.
\Next actions from our side:
- I'll return the completed questionnaire with notes on key rotation (attached).
